(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.description: A vertigo condition that causes brief episodes of spinning dizziness triggered by head movement.

AIDS.description: A chronic viral infection that weakens the immune system over time.

Acne.description: A common skin condition involving clogged pores and inflammatory lesions.

Alcoholic hepatitis.description: Inflammation of the liver caused by heavy alcohol use.

Allergy.description: An immune reaction to substances such as pollen, dust, or food.

Arthritis.description: Inflammation of joints leading to pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility.

Bronchial Asthma.description: A chronic airway condition that makes breathing difficult.

Cervical spondylosis.description: Wear-and-tear changes in the cervical spine that can cause neck pain and stiffness.

Chicken pox.description: A contagious viral infection that causes an itchy blister-like rash.

Chronic cholestasis.description: A chronic reduction in bile flow that can cause jaundice and itching.

Common Cold.description: A viral upper respiratory infection that usually improves with rest and fluids.

Dengue.description: A mosquito-borne viral illness that can become severe if not monitored carefully.

Diabetes.description: A metabolic condition characterized by elevated blood sugar.

Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).description: Swollen veins in the rectal area that can cause pain and bleeding.

Drug Reaction.description: An adverse reaction to a medication that may affect the skin or other organs.

Fungal infection.description: A fungal skin infection commonly presenting with itchy rashes and irritation.

GERD.description: Gastroesophageal reflux disease, where stomach acid flows back into the esophagus.

Gastroenteritis.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines causing vomiting and diarrhea.

Heart attack.description: A medical emergency caused by blocked blood flow to the heart muscle.

Hepatitis B.description: A viral liver infection that can become chronic and cause liver damage.

Hepatitis C.description: A viral liver infection that can cause long-term liver complications.

Hepatitis D.description: A liver infection that occurs in people already infected with hepatitis B.

Hepatitis E.description: A viral liver infection often spread through contaminated water.

Hypertension.description: Persistently elevated blood pressure that can increase cardiovascular risk.

Hyperthyroidism.description: An overactive thyroid gland that speeds up many body functions.

Hypoglycemia.description: A low blood sugar condition that can become dangerous if severe.

Hypothyroidism.description: A condition in which the thyroid gland produces insufficient hormones.

Impetigo.description: A contagious bacterial skin infection that causes sores and crusting.

Jaundice.description: Yellowing of the skin and eyes caused by elevated bilirubin.

Malaria.description: A mosquito-borne infectious disease that can cause cyclical fever and chills.

Migraine.description: A recurrent headache disorder that can be accompanied by nausea and visual symptoms.

Osteoarthristis.description: A degenerative joint condition that causes pain and stiffness.

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).description: A serious neurological condition that can cause sudden weakness or paralysis.

Peptic ulcer diseae.description: An ulcer in the stomach or upper intestine that can cause pain and digestive symptoms.

Pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs.

Psoriasis.description: A chronic inflammatory skin disease causing scaly plaques.

Tuberculosis.description: A contagious bacterial infection that commonly affects the lungs.

Typhoid.description: A bacterial infection that can cause high fever and abdominal symptoms.

Urinary tract infection.description: An infection in the urinary system that can cause pain and frequent urination.

Varicose veins.description: Enlarged, twisted veins that often affect the legs.

hepatitis A.description: A viral liver infection usually spread through contaminated food or water.
